argmax.description: Exact accepted vocabulary selection and generated-token state update. Inputs: float32 scores [248320], int64 tokens [S], integer decision d in [0,S). Outputs: rank-zero int64 selected index and complete int64 tokens [S], in fresh storage, with only tokens[d] replaced. Each of 512 blocks scans 485 entries using eight logical lanes spaced by eight, initializes all 32 logical lanes, then reduces at distances 16,8,4,2,1 and blocks at 256,128,...,1. The exact better predicate accepts a valid index if the incumbent is invalid, the value is strictly larger, or it is NaN and the incumbent is not. Equal values and equal NaN status retain the incumbent in this traversal/tree order, not a generic lowest-index tie rule. No score arithmetic or parallel reduction. This is its own proof target; exact replay is not a proof of upstream score equivalence or argmax stability under approximately related scores.

attention_decoder.description: One complete accepted full-attention decoder layer: pre/post RMS norms, Q/gate/K/V projections, head RMS norms and partial rotary transform, bfloat16 KV-cache writes, grouped-query attention with the original sixteen logical-warp online-softmax partitions and merge order, sigmoid head gating, output projection, both residual bfloat16 roundings, and gated MLP. Inputs: packed bfloat16 weights, float32 hidden [1024], complete bfloat16 keys/values (each [6,2,2048,256]), float32 cosine/sine (each [32]), integer weight base, integer cache slot fa in [0,6), integer position in [0,2048). The weight interval [base,base+18352640) must exist. Prior positions of this slot must contain the supplied sequence's KV state. Outputs: float32 hidden [1024], complete bfloat16 keys and values in fresh storage; only this slot's current position is changed. Recurrent/convolution and token/history state pass via unchanged graph bindings. Preserve all PTX approximations, dot/sum/softmax/FMA orders and bfloat16 casts; one physical thread, matching the accepted non-tensor-core implementation.

embedding.description: Accepted active-position token selection, embedding load, and rotary setup. Inputs: bfloat16 embedding table [248320,1024], int64 prompt [L], int64 generated-token state [S], integer position p with 0<=p<min(12,L+S-1); selected token IDs must be in [0,248320). Position zero reads tokens[0], later prompt positions read prompt[p], and generated positions read tokens[p-L]. Outputs: float32 hidden [1024], cosine [32], sine [32]. Preserve runtime div/lg2/ex2/cos/sin approximate FTZ instructions and unroll-1 rotary loop; do not constant-fold the powers. One physical thread. All persistent state, tokens/history, immutable weights/prompt, and position remain explicit graph bindings; values not modified by a family remain bound to their preceding producer.

final_projection.description: Accepted generation-only final RMS normalization and tied vocabulary projection, including the existing hidden-history write. Inputs: bfloat16 embedding/output table [248320,1024], bfloat16 final norm weights [1024], float32 post-layer hidden [1024], bfloat16 full history [S,1024], integer decision d in [0,S). Outputs: all float32 scores [248320] and full bfloat16 history [S,1024], in fresh storage. History row d receives the pre-final-norm hidden; other rows are copied. Final normalized values remain float32, unlike decoder pre/post norms. Retain the continuous-dot accumulation and b/w/m score traversal from the fused projection/running maximum. Instrumentation stores each score immediately after its original computation while leaving all original comparisons intact. Argmax is a separate family; this numerical target makes no index-stability or cross-implementation equivalence claim. One physical thread.

inactive_decode.description: The accepted decode_step early-return branch, not an invented epilogue. Inputs: full float32 recurrent [18,16,128,128] and convolution [18,6144,4] state, full bfloat16 keys/values [6,2,2048,256], int64 tokens [S], bfloat16 history [S,1024], integer position p, integer prompt length L. Preconditions: L>0, S>0 and L+S-1<=p<12. Outputs are fresh copies of all six state tensors in input order, with unchanged dtype and shape. Preserve the original serial copy order (KV, tokens, history, recurrent state, convolution state). Every inactive fixed launch is scheduled and independently observed, including all state, not only the two externally returned tensors.

initialize.description: The accepted standalone initialize kernel, not an invented prologue. Inputs: contiguous CUDA int64 prompt [L], generation count S (1..12), L>0. One physical thread initializes every value of float32 recurrent state [18,16,128,128], float32 four-tap convolution state [18,6144,4], bfloat16 keys and values (each [6,2,2048,256]), int64 tokens [S], and bfloat16 history [S,1024]. All begin at zero except tokens[0]=prompt[0]. Outputs are those six tensors, in that order, in fresh storage. The schedule retains all twelve original decode launches, including inactive ones.

recurrent_decoder.description: One complete accepted recurrent decoder layer, including pre/post RMS norms, QKV/Z/beta/alpha projections, four-tap causal convolution and SiLU, normalized Q/K, delta recurrence with softplus/decay, gated output norm, output projection, both residual bfloat16 roundings, and gated MLP. Inputs: packed bfloat16 weights, float32 hidden [1024], complete float32 recurrent state [18,16,128,128], complete float32 convolution state [18,6144,4], integer weight base, integer recurrent slot dn in [0,18). The weight interval [base,base+21555360) must exist and have the accepted packed layout. Outputs: hidden [1024], full recurrent state, full convolution state, all float32 and in fresh storage. Only slot dn is changed; other slots are copied exactly. The trace records the actual in-kernel live frontier: already-updated slots from state_out/conv_out and not-yet-updated slots from state_in/conv_in. KV, rotary, token/history state remain live through unchanged graph bindings. Keep grouped versus continuous dot accumulation, logical 32-lane/512-thread sum trees, PTX FTZ arithmetic, and every original rounding. This accepted implementation uses one physical thread and no tensor-core instructions.
